llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: L-ascorbic acid is treated as the solid analyte and is dispensed directly into the experiment vial by Quantos before water addition and mixing. It is not assigned to a liquid pump channel and no pre-prepared Vitamin C solution is assumed. To minimize oxidation, the solution should be prepared fresh, protected from unnecessary light exposure, and transferred to electrochemical measurement immediately after mixing and pH measurement.
assumptions: Solid KCl and solid L-ascorbic acid are physically available for loading into separate Quantos cartridges; these reagents must be loaded before execution.
Water is available as a pump-compatible liquid on syringe-pump channel 1.
The stated molecular weight of Vitamin C refers to anhydrous L-ascorbic acid, C6H8O6, with molecular weight 176.124 g/mol.
The stated molecular weight of KCl is 74.5513 g/mol.
The 7.000 mL preparation volume is sufficient for the electrochemical substation cell configuration.

The platform will measure and record pH before and after CV using its available pH-measurement capability, although pH adjustment is not included because no compatible acid/base reagent or pH target was specified.
The actual delivered solid mass accuracy is governed by Quantos performance; reported actual concentrations are nominal values calculated from planned masses.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: Required KCl moles = 0.100 mol/L × 0.007000 L = 0.0007000 mol. Theoretical mass = 0.0007000 mol × 74.5513 g/mol = 0.05218591 g = 52.18591 mg. The planned Quantos mass is rounded to 52.186 mg. Nominal concentration from the planned mass is (0.052186 g / 74.5513 g/mol) / 0.007000 L = 0.10000017 mol/L.

Required Vitamin C moles = 0.00500 mol/L × 0.007000 L = 0.00003500 mol. Theoretical mass = 0.00003500 mol × 176.124 g/mol = 0.00616434 g = 6.16434 mg. The planned Quantos mass is rounded to 6.164 mg. Nominal concentration from the planned mass is (0.006164 g / 176.124 g/mol) / 0.007000 L = 0.00499972 mol/L.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: The plan uses 2 solid cartridges, which is within the maximum of 8, and 1 liquid pump channel, which is within the maximum of 4. Each solid mass is below the 200 mg per-cartridge Quantos capacity: KCl is 52.186 mg and Vitamin C is 6.164 mg. The 7.000 mL water volume equals 7000 uL, which is exactly 1000 increments of 7 uL and is therefore compatible with the liquid dispenser. The final volume is 7.000 mL, below the 10 mL vial limit. One electrochemical slot is used, below the maximum of 3. Both solids are assigned to Quantos cartridges and water is the only liquid assigned to the solvent pump. Mixing follows all solid additions.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: No analyte film is deposited on the working electrode; therefore, no post-deposition drying step is required. Electrode washing and drying after polishing remain required before immersion in the freshly prepared electrolyte.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: No electrode deposition is performed because the analyte is dissolved in the electrolyte. Before measurement, the available gold working electrode should be polished for 3 polishing cycles, washed, dried, and installed with the platinum counter electrode and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Dispense 52.186 mg KCl from Quantos cartridge position 1 and 6.164 mg L-ascorbic acid from Quantos cartridge position 2 into one clean experiment vial. Dispense 7.000 mL water through pump channel 1. Insert/use the vial stir bar and mix for 120 seconds until the solids are fully dissolved. Measure and record the solution pH before the CV test using the available pH capability. Nitrogen-purge the prepared electrolyte immediately before measurement. The prepared solution is nominally 0.1000 M KCl and 5.00 mM Vitamin C.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.100 M KCl aqueous supporting electrolyte provides ionic conductivity without introducing a strongly electroactive supporting salt in the selected potential region. A nominal 5.00 mM L-ascorbic acid concentration provides a readily measurable oxidation response while using a small solid mass within the Quantos cartridge limit. The -0.20 to 0.80 V window versus Ag/AgCl is selected to observe ascorbic-acid oxidation on gold while limiting unnecessarily positive excursions. A 0.050 V/s scan rate and 2 mV step size provide conventional characterization resolution. Three cycles permit observation of first-cycle surface effects and subsequent response stabilization. Nitrogen purging is selected to reduce dissolved-oxygen reduction/oxidation interference. The sample should be measured immediately after preparation because Vitamin C is susceptible to oxidative degradation.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The requested experiment is analite_in_electrolite because Vitamin C is to be dissolved directly in a supporting electrolyte inside the experiment vial rather than deposited on the gold working electrode.

metadata.description: Vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid) dissolved in an aqueous 0.100 M KCl supporting electrolyte and characterized by cyclic voltammetry using a gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.

cross_contamination_risks: Vitamin C oxidation products may adsorb on the gold working electrode and alter subsequent voltammograms.
KCl residue can contaminate later low-ionic-strength experiments.
Mitigate carryover by washing and drying electrodes and using the platform water-wash vials after the experiment.
handling_precautions: Load KCl and Vitamin C into separate labeled Quantos cartridges while minimizing powder generation.
Wear laboratory coat, safety glasses, and suitable gloves during cartridge loading and waste handling.
Use freshly loaded Vitamin C and prepare the solution immediately before analysis because aqueous ascorbic acid can oxidize during storage and exposure to air or light.
Mix until all solids are dissolved before purging and CV measurement.
Use the nitrogen purge in a ventilated enclosure and avoid directing nitrogen toward personnel.
Polish, wash, and dry the gold working electrode before the measurement to minimize surface-fouling and carryover effects.
hazards: Potassium chloride and L-ascorbic acid are low-hazard solids but may cause mild eye, skin, or respiratory irritation as powders.
Nitrogen purging can create a localized oxygen-deficient atmosphere if used in an inadequately ventilated enclosure.

The electrochemical cell contains an Ag/AgCl reference electrode and platinum counter electrode; reference-electrode leakage or damaged electrodes must be treated as metal-containing laboratory waste.
waste_disposal: Collect the post-CV KCl/Vitamin C electrolyte as aqueous electrochemical waste; do not return it to reagent containers.
If reference-electrode electrolyte leakage is suspected, segregate the solution as silver-containing waste according to local procedures.
Dispose of contaminated wipes, polishing media, and rinse solutions according to the laboratory's chemical-waste procedures.
